title: nf-core/proteinfamilies pipeline parameters
description: Generate protein family level models (Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs), Hidden Markov Models (HMMs)) starting from a FASTA amino acid sequence file.

input_output_options.title: Input/output options
input_output_options.description: Define where the pipeline should find input data and save output data.

input.description: Path to comma-separated file '.csv' containing information about the samples in the experiment.
input.help_text: You will need to create a design file with information about the samples in your experiment before running the pipeline. Use this parameter to specify its location. It has to be a comma-separated file '.csv' with 2 mandatory and 3 optional columns, and a header row. See [usage docs](https://nf-co.re/proteinfamilies/usage#samplesheet-input).

outdir.description: The output directory where the results will be saved. You have to use absolute paths to storage on Cloud infrastructure.
outdir.help_text: You will need to define where your results will be saved. Use this parameter to specify the location.

email.description: Email address for completion summary. Example: name.surname@example.com
email.help_text: Set this parameter to your e-mail address to get a summary e-mail with details of the run sent to you when the workflow exits. If set in your user config file (`~/.nextflow/config`) then you don't need to specify this on the command line for every run.

multiqc_title.description: MultiQC report title. Printed as page header, used for filename if not otherwise specified.

save_intermediates.description: Publish intermediate files under `intermediates/` (e.g. clustering databases, raw alignments and HMMs, search results).
save_intermediates.help_text: Final results are always published (`families/<id>/`, `qc/`, `clustering/`, `phylogeny/`); intermediate files only with this flag. Useful for debugging or to inspect each step's files.

institutional_config_options.title: Institutional config options
institutional_config_options.description: Parameters used to describe centralised config profiles. These should not be edited.
institutional_config_options.help_text: The centralised nf-core configuration profiles use a handful of pipeline parameters to describe themselves. This information is then printed to the Nextflow log when you run a pipeline. You should not need to change these values when you run a pipeline.

custom_config_version.description: Git commit id for Institutional configs.

custom_config_base.help_text: If you're running offline, Nextflow will not be able to fetch the institutional config files from the internet. If you don't need them, then this is not a problem. If you do need them, you should download the files from the repo and tell Nextflow where to find them with this parameter.

modules_testdata_base_path.description: Base path / URL for data used in the modules

generic_options.title: Generic options
generic_options.description: Less common options for the pipeline, typically set in a config file.
generic_options.help_text:
These options are common to all nf-core pipelines and allow you to customise some of the core preferences for how the pipeline runs.

Typically these options would be set in a Nextflow config file loaded for all pipeline runs, such as `~/.nextflow/config`.

publish_dir_mode.description: Method used to save pipeline results to output directory.
publish_dir_mode.help_text: The Nextflow `publishDir` option specifies which intermediate files should be saved to the output directory. This option tells the pipeline what method should be used to move these files. See [Nextflow docs](https://www.nextflow.io/docs/latest/process.html#publishdir) for details.

email_on_fail.description: Email address for completion summary, only when pipeline fails. Example: name.surname@example.com
email_on_fail.help_text: An email address to send a summary email to when the pipeline is completed - ONLY sent if the pipeline does not exit successfully.

plaintext_email.description: Send plain-text email instead of HTML.

max_multiqc_email_size.description: File size limit when attaching MultiQC reports to summary emails. Example: name.surname@example.com

monochrome_logs.description: Do not use coloured log outputs.

multiqc_config.description: Custom config file to supply to MultiQC.

multiqc_logo.description: Custom logo file to supply to MultiQC. File name must also be set in the MultiQC config file

multiqc_methods_description.description: Custom MultiQC yaml file containing HTML including a methods description.

validate_params.description: Boolean whether to validate parameters against the schema at runtime

pipelines_testdata_base_path.description: Base URL or local path to location of pipeline test dataset files

trace_report_suffix.description: Suffix to add to the trace report filename. Default is the date and time in the format yyyy-MM-dd_HH-mm-ss.

help_full.description: Display the full detailed help message.

show_hidden.description: Display hidden parameters in the help message (only works when --help or --help_full are provided).

quality_check_params.title: Preprocessing parameters
quality_check_params.description: Use these parameters to control the quality check and preprocessing of the input sequences.

skip_preprocessing.description: Skip all default QC steps for sequences (gap trimming, length filtering, validation, duplicate removal).
skip_preprocessing.help: Skips input amino acid sequence preprocessing transformations, length filtering, duplicate removal and validation checks.

min_seq_length.help_text: Specify the minimum length of amino acid sequences that go into clustering.

max_seq_length.help_text: Specify the maximum length of amino acid sequences that go into clustering.

deduplicate_by.description: How duplicate input sequences are found and removed.
deduplicate_by.help_text: `name` (default): sequences with the same identifier are duplicates. `sequence`: sequences with the same amino acid sequence are duplicates, whatever their names.

clustering_params.title: Clustering parameters
clustering_params.description: Use these parameters to control the initial clustering of the input sequences.

clustering_tool.description: Choose clustering algorithm. Either simple 'cluster' for medium size inputs, or 'linclust' for less sensitive clustering of larger datasets.

clustering_min_seq_identity.description: mmseqs parameter for minimum sequence identity
clustering_min_seq_identity.help_text: Minimum sequence identity required for clustering. Metagenomics protein families include diverse sequences, so using the mmseqs default identity (0.9) would oversplit them. A default value of 0.3 allows grouping more distant homologs while still maintaining meaningful functional relationships (https://doi.org/10.1093/protein/12.2.85).

clustering_min_coverage.description: mmseqs parameter for minimum sequence coverage ratio
clustering_min_coverage.help_text: Minimum sequence length coverage required for clustering. Similarly to the clustering_min_seq_identity parameter, a lower value (i.e., 0.5) than the mmseqs default (i.e., 0.8) enables the generation of protein families that are composed of more distant homologs.

clustering_cov_mode.description: mmseqs parameter for coverage mode: 0 for both, 1 for target and 2 for query sequence
clustering_cov_mode.help_text: Defined by the number of aligned residue pairs divided by 0: the maximum of the length of query/centre and target/non-centre sequences, 1: the length of the target/non-centre sequence, 2: the length of the query/centre

clustering_min_cluster_size.description: Minimum clustering chunk size threshold to create seed Multiple Sequence Alignments upon.
clustering_min_cluster_size.help_text: This is an initial filter for the mmseqs clustering results. The lower the threshold, the more families will be generated. Additional sequences may be later recruited in the families.

family_generation_params.title: Family generation parameters
family_generation_params.description: Use these parameters to choose and control the family generation algorithm, and the update of existing families.

family_generation_algorithm.description: Choose the algorithm that turns clusters into family models. Either 'standard', aligning each cluster and building one HMM per task, or 'iterative', letting mgnifam loop HMM building, recruitment and realignment per cluster.
family_generation_algorithm.help_text: The 'standard' algorithm chains FAMSA/MAFFT, ClipKIT, hmmbuild, hmmsearch and hmmalign, and recruits members in a single pass. The 'iterative' algorithm runs mgnifam, which uses pyfamsa, pytrimal and pyhmmer internally and repeats recruitment and realignment up to 3 iterations, or until each family converges or is discarded. Not all alignment and recruitment parameters of the standard algorithm apply to the iterative one; see the usage documentation for the full mapping.

iterative_clusters_per_chunk.description: Number of clusters handed to each family generation task by the 'iterative' algorithm.
iterative_clusters_per_chunk.help_text: Only used when family_generation_algorithm is 'iterative', which generates many families per task. Smaller chunks parallelise better and resume at a finer granularity, at the cost of more tasks. The 'standard' algorithm always processes a single cluster per task.

alignment_tool.description: Choose alignment tool. FAMSA is recommended as best time-memory-accuracy combination option.

skip_update_refinement.description: Keep the existing HMMs of updated families, only rebuilding their full MSAs.
skip_update_refinement.help_text: By default, each updated family is rebuilt from its hits like a newly created family: new seed MSA, new HMM, and a full MSA recruited with the new HMM. With this flag, the existing HMM is kept and aligns its hits (from the input sequences and the members of any existing full MSAs) into the new full MSA with hmmalign; a provided seed MSA passes through unchanged, otherwise the family has no seed MSA. Updated families are then never merged with similar families (as with `--family_merging created_only`), since a merge would rebuild their HMM.

seed_msa_trimming_params.title: Seed MSA trimming parameters
seed_msa_trimming_params.description: Use these parameters to control the trimming of the seed multiple sequence alignments.

skip_seed_msa_trimming.description: Skip trimming gappy positions from seed Multiple Sequence Alignments (MSAs). Full MSAs are never trimmed.

seed_msa_trimming_ends_only.description: Choose if ClipKIT should only clip gaps at the ends of the MSAs.
seed_msa_trimming_ends_only.help_text: By default, ClipKIT clips gaps over the specified threshold, both at the ends and throughout the length of the MSA. This flag restricts clipping to the ends. The pipeline authors strongly recommend keeping this on: trimmed rows get their `name/start-end` coordinates recalculated from the residues removed at the alignment ends, so with interior trimming the range no longer matches the residues a row holds.

seed_msa_trimming_max_gap_fraction.description: Multiple Sequence Alignment (MSA) positions with gappiness greater than this threshold will be trimmed

recruiting_params.title: Recruiting and search parameters
recruiting_params.description: Use these parameters to control the HMM searches and the recruitment of additional sequences into the families.

skip_recruiting.description: Skip recruitment of additional sequences from the input FASTA file using the family Hidden Markov Models (HMMs) into the full alignment
skip_recruiting.help_text: If this is set to false, the hmmer/hmmsearch module will be used to recruit additional sequences from the input fasta file into the family (above the recruit_min_model_coverage), resulting in bigger but better described families

search_evalue_cutoff.description: hmmsearch e-value cutoff threshold for reported results

recruit_min_model_coverage.description: hmmsearch minimum length percentage filter of hit env vs query length
recruit_min_model_coverage.help_text: This length threshold should be quite high to make sure that small, fragmented sequences are not recruited in the family models

family_redundancy_params.title: Family redundancy parameters
family_redundancy_params.description: Use these parameters to control the removal of redundant families and the merging of similar families.

family_redundancy_removal.description: Which families take part in the removal of between-family redundancy (hmmsearch of family representatives against family models).
family_redundancy_removal.help_text: `all` (default): created and updated families are checked. An updated family is never removed: a created family redundant with it is, and two redundant updated families are both kept. `created_only`: updated families bypass the check, so created families may duplicate them. `none`: no family is removed for redundancy. Suggested to keep `all`, so that redundant families are not further processed, for better resource management and to avoid duplication.

family_merging.description: Which families can be merged with similar (but not redundant) families.
family_merging.help_text: Similarity is set by `--family_similarity_min_model_coverage`. `all` (default): created and updated families can be merged. A merge pool holds at most one updated family: two updated families are never merged together, and a pool that links several updated families (directly or through created families) leaves them unmerged and merges only its created families. `created_only`: updated families are left out of merging. `none`: no family is merged. With `--skip_update_refinement`, updated families are never merged (as with `created_only`), since a merge rebuilds the family's HMM.

merged_family_name.description: Name of a merged family that holds updated families.
merged_family_name.help_text: `existing` keeps the name of the merged updated family (a merge holds at most one), so the family keeps its identity across updates. `new` names the merged family like any other merge, after the sample and its families. Applies to `--family_generation_algorithm standard`; the iterative algorithm always uses `new`.

family_redundancy_min_model_coverage.description: hmmsearch minimum length percentage filter of hit env vs query length, for redundant family removal

family_similarity_min_model_coverage.description: hmmsearch minimum length percentage of hit env vs query length, to flag and report similar families (and to optionally merge)
family_similarity_min_model_coverage.help_text: Must be below the family_redundancy_min_model_coverage to be valid.

seq_redundancy_params.title: Sequence redundancy parameters
seq_redundancy_params.description: Use these parameters to control the removal of redundant sequences within each family.

skip_sequence_redundancy_removal.description: Skip removal of inside-family redundancy of sequences via mmseqs clustering.
skip_sequence_redundancy_removal.help_text: Highly similar sequences within the same family should be removed, while making sure that the protein family diversity is still well captured.

seq_redundancy_min_seq_identity.description: mmseqs parameter for minimum sequence identity
seq_redundancy_min_seq_identity.help_text: Need to be quite high, to make sure that the diversity is still well captured, while highly similar sequences are removed

seq_redundancy_min_coverage.description: mmseqs parameter for minimum sequence coverage ratio
seq_redundancy_min_coverage.help_text: Need to be quite high, to make sure that the diversity is still well captured, well highly similar sequences are removed

seq_redundancy_cov_mode.description: mmseqs parameter for coverage mode: 0 for both, 1 for target and 2 for query sequence
seq_redundancy_cov_mode.help_text: Defined by the number of aligned residue pairs divided by 0: the maximum of the length of query/centre and target/non-centre sequences, 1: the length of the target/non-centre sequence, 2: the length of the query/centre

phylogeny_params.title: Parameters for phylogenetic inference of full alignment sequences
phylogeny_params.description: Use these parameters to enable the phylogenetic tree construction of the final full MSAs.

run_phylogenetic_inference.description: Infer a phylogenetic tree of each final family's full MSA with CMAPLE.
